inlines.v: CONSOLIDATE, verb transitive [Latin , solid. See Solid.] 1. To make solid to unite or press together loose or separate parts, and form a compact mass; to harden or make dense and firm. He fixed and consolidated the earth above the waters. 2. To unite the parts of a broken bone or the lips of a wound, by means of applications. 3. To unite two parliamentary bills in one. 4. In law, to combine two benefices in one. CONSOLIDATE, verb intransitive To grow firm and hard; to unite and become solid. In hurts and ulcers of the head, dryness maketh them more apt to consolidate Moist clay consolidates by drying. CONSOLIDATE, adjective Formed into a solid mass.
